record.context_brief: Sarkozy Problem 67 on ternary sums from dense prime subsets
record.original_question: If Q = {q1, q2, ...} is an infinite set of primes satisfying lim inf_{x -> infinity} (log x / x) |{qi : qi <= x, qi in Q}| > 1/2, does every sufficiently large odd integer 2n + 1 admit a representation qi + qj + qk = 2n + 1 with qi, qj, qk in Q?

evidence.quote: Problem 67. Is it true that if Q = {q1, q2, . . .} is an infinite set of primes such that lim inf x->infinity (log x / x) |{qi : qi <= x, qi in Q}| > 1/2, then every large odd integer 2n + 1 can be represented in the form qi + qj + qk = 2n + 1 (with qi, qj, qk in Q)?
In [20] Yang and Togbe answered negatively Problem 67 and obtained more explicit results on this problem.

Theorem 2. There is an infinite set Q of primes with upper relative prime density 1 and lower relative prime density 5/8 such that there are infinitely many odd integers 2n + 1 that cannot be represented as q1 + q2 + q3 = 2n + 1 with qi in Q (1 <= i <= 3).

artifact.category_tag: ternary Goldbach in dense prime subsets
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the set of all prime numbers. For a set $Q = \{q_1, q_2, \dots\} \subseteq \mathcal{P}$, define the lower relative prime density of $Q$ as
$$\underline{d}(Q) = \liminf_{x \to \infty} \frac{\log x}{x}\,\bigl|\{q \in Q : q \le x\}\bigr|.$$
(Note that by the prime number theorem, $\underline{d}(\mathcal{P}) = 1$.)

Question: Is it true that whenever $Q \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ is an infinite set of primes satisfying
$$\underline{d}(Q) > \tfrac{1}{2},$$
every sufficiently large odd integer $2n+1$ can be written as
$$q_i + q_j + q_k = 2n+1$$
with $q_i, q_j, q_k \in Q$ (not necessarily distinct)?

Decide whether the implication holds, or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved negatively. A construction produces an infinite set of primes with upper relative prime density 1 and lower relative prime density 5/8 such that infinitely many odd integers cannot be written as a sum of three primes from the set, refuting the conjectured implication.

status_evidence.title: Yang–Togbé on Sárközy's Problem 67
status_evidence.snippet: There is an infinite set Q of primes with upper relative prime density 1 and lower relative prime density 5/8 such that there are infinitely many odd integers 2n+1 that cannot be represented as q1+q2+q3.
status_evidence.claim: A counterexample with lower relative density 5/8 refutes the conjecture.
